quadratics.description:
Be able to answer any Quadratics question on Paper 1 without notes.

Key points:
• Complete the square and read off the vertex and line of symmetry
• Use the discriminant b² − 4ac for two, one or no real roots
• Solve quadratic inequalities with a sketch
• Solve a linear and a quadratic equation simultaneously
• Solve equations that are quadratic in a function of x, e.g. in x² or √x
• Use the discriminant for a line that is tangent to a curve

How: For each key point, rework one example from your notes or textbook, then cover the answer and do it again from memory. Write down any formula you had to look up.

First step: Open your notes on Quadratics and redo one example for the first key point without looking.

mapped.name: Cambridge International AS Level Chemistry (9701), Paper 2
units: Atomic structure: Define and calculate ionisation energies for successive electrons; Explain trends in ionisation energy across periods and down groups
Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry: Calculate moles, masses, concentrations and gas volumes; Determine empirical and molecular formulae
Chemical bonding: Describe ionic, covalent and metallic bonding; Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for molecules and ions
States of matter: Describe the solid, liquid and gas states and changes between them; Explain properties of solids by structure and bonding
Chemical energetics: Define enthalpy changes of reaction, formation and combustion; Use Hess's law and energy cycles
Electrochemistry: Use standard electrode potentials to predict redox reactions; Write cell diagrams and calculate standard cell emf
Equilibria: Apply Le Chatelier's principle to gaseous and solution equilibria; Write and calculate Kc and Kp expressions
Reaction kinetics: Explain rates in terms of collision theory; Interpret Maxwell-Boltzmann distributions
The Periodic Table: Describe trends in Group 2 and their reactions with water and oxygen; Explain trends in Group 17 reactivity and displacement reactions
Chemical periodicity: Explain trends in physical properties across Period 3; Explain trends in oxides and chlorides of Period 3 elements
Nitrogen and sulfur: Describe reactions and properties of ammonia and ammonium compounds; Explain the chemistry of nitrogen oxides as pollutants
Introduction to organic chemistry: Name compounds using IUPAC nomenclature; Identify functional groups and classify reactions
Hydrocarbons: Describe free radical substitution of alkanes; Explain electrophilic addition to alkenes with mechanisms
Halogen compounds: Draw nucleophilic substitution mechanisms (SN1/SN2); Explain rates of hydrolysis of haloalkanes
Hydroxy compounds: Describe reactions of alcohols with sodium, oxidising agents and halide ions; Distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols
Carbonyl compounds: Describe nucleophilic addition with HCN and its mechanism; Use 2,4-DNP, Tollens' and Fehling's reagents for identification
Carboxylic acids and derivatives: Describe reactions of carboxylic acids to make esters and salts; Describe hydrolysis of esters and nitriles
